clue.text: Old money collection hidden among vegetables

indicators.note: the collection is tucked away within the vegetables, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: peas are vegetables
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: Some old coins have been squirrelled away in the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden among' looks like a signal for letters concealed in the clue's own words, but here it is an insertion of one synonym inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the Spanish currency before the euro replaced it, so it is old money.

clue.text: Step round city's grand building

indicators.note: the step word goes round the city

parts.note: a pace is a step
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Walking around a city to see its fine architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the grand residence of a monarch or bishop.

clue.text: Right up inside smooth thread

indicators.note: the right letters sit inside the smooth word

parts.note: to sand is to smooth a surface

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Pulling a thread up through fabric to make it smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a single thread or fibre, as in a strand of hair.

clue.text: Cutter sail, possibly nut-related?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a boat's sail has anything to do with nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' is slang for the male gonads, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is a slang term for the male reproductive glands, so a slang reading of nut-related fits.

clue.text: Son biting Dawn?

parts.note: tart means sharp or biting in taste

explanation.surface: A boy bites a woman named Dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a woman's name; it is the start of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the beginning of the day, so it is an example of a beginning.

clue.text: Fellow American needs genuine protection? No

indicators.note: the genuine word wraps round and shields the other pieces, like a protective cover

parts.note: genuine means real
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: An American man asks for real security, and the answer comes back negative.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and the stray 'No' make the definition hard to spot: it is the single last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is a refusal, a rejection of a request or offer.

clue.text: Novel chap who likes the company of travelling folk, cod mornay and whiskey

definitions.text: Novel chap who likes the company of travelling folk

indicators.note: cod means fake or mock, so the letters of mornay are faked into a new order

parts.note: rye is an American whiskey

explanation.surface: A traveller's friend dines on cod mornay with a glass of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' looks like part of the dish but is the anagram signal. George Borrow's novel is The Romany Rye; the term means a gentleman who keeps company with Gypsies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Borrow's usage a rye is a gentleman who associates with Gypsy people, the title of his novel.

clue.text: Part of Arthurian windbreak

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something from King Arthur's legend that shelters people from wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windbreak' is normally a screen; here it is read as breaking wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking wind is a polite phrase for passing gas, which this rude word names.

clue.text: Not a natural place to bathe, or sail off with a flipping Greek character

definitions.text: Not a natural place to bathe

indicators.note: the letters are off, out of their proper order
the Greek letter is flipped, read upwards in this down light

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Advice to sail away with a wretched Greek rather than swim in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A solarium is a room with sunlamps for tanning, so sunbathing there is artificial.

clue.text: No professional team obscures a save …

indicators.note: the amateur team hides the letter a inside itself

parts.note: lay means amateur, not professional
a side is a team

explanation.surface: An amateur side blocks a shot at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 13 down; this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside for later is to save it.

clue.text: Look at ways to get peers assembled

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
RDS abbreviates roads, which are ways

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch how members of the peerage gather together.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lords is the chamber where the peers of the realm sit together.

clue.text: Butterfly on empty tray that represents sailors

parts.note: the red admiral and white admiral are butterflies

indicators.note: an empty tray has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A butterfly settles on a bare tray that serves as some naval emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiralty was the British government department in charge of the Royal Navy, so it stood for the navy's seamen.

clue.text: Steady relative in happy surroundings

indicators.note: the relative is placed in the other piece
the happy word forms the surroundings that enclose the relative

parts.note: happy means content
sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative who is kept calm by a cheerful setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consistent is steady and unchanging in its behaviour.

clue.text: God is angry on being overthrown

indicators.note: a word that is overthrown is turned upside down, read back to front in an across light

parts.note: sore can mean angry, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: A deity is furious at being toppled from power.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, the counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: … before strained situation leads to unjustified claim

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
tension is a strained state of affairs

explanation.surface: A tense atmosphere leads someone to make a false claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretension is a claim to a merit or status one does not really have.

clue.text: Resistance movement not fully crushed

parts.note: under as a prefix means not fully, as in undercooked
ground means crushed, as coffee beans are

explanation.surface: A rebel group has been only partly defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Underground is the name for a secret resistance organisation, such as the French one in the Second World War.

clue.text: Leach land freely to create suitable environment for hops

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters are set loose in any order

explanation.surface: Letting the soil drain freely gives hop plants good conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Hops look like the plant used in brewing; here they are dances, as in a sock hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop is an informal dance, and a dance hall is where dances are held.

clue.text: Peripheral dictionary includes 'indicative of something to come'

indicators.note: the two words include the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A minor dictionary has an entry for a word about portents.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in quotation marks to look like a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald announces something coming, so heraldic can describe a sign that foreshadows events.

clue.text: Pieces of furniture with hollow body supports

parts.note: sticks of furniture are individual pieces

indicators.note: a hollow body has its inside removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Chairs and tables with an empty frame keep someone upright.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick by someone is to remain loyal and supportive.

clue.text: Rail passengers go through this diversion, losing energy and time

indicators.note: the diversion word loses the letters for energy and time from inside it

parts.note: entertainment is a diversion or amusement
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Travellers on a train are kept amused, though they get tired and run late.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking E and T out of ENTERTAINMENT leaves ENTRAINMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train, so passengers going aboard undergo the process of getting on.

clue.text: Restless type able to swallow date, say, upside down

indicators.note: the able word swallows the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: fit means able, as in fit for work

indicators.note: in a down light, upside down reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: An agitated person who can gulp down a date fruit while standing on their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' applies only to 'say', not to the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidget is someone who cannot keep still.

clue.text: Bluish-grey bench one removed from row

parts.note: a pew is a bench in church

indicators.note: the letter for one is removed from the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grey church bench is taken out of a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewter is a tin alloy whose dull grey shade gives its name to a colour.

clue.text: Vault tree, avoiding lake

indicators.note: the tree word avoids, or does without, the letter for lake

parts.note: the larch is a conifer tree
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An instruction to leap over a tree without landing in the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' reads as a verb, to jump, but it is the curved roof structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is a curved roof built from arches, so an arch is a type of vault.

clue.text: Winding river engulfs inept punter (university dropout)

indicators.note: the river swallows up the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris

indicators.note: an inept punter fumbles, so the letters are jumbled
the university letter drops out of the word punter

explanation.surface: A clumsy boatman on a river, a student who quit his studies, is swept away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropout' takes U out of the punter, and 'inept' then rearranges what is left into RPENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine describes something twisting like a snake, the same as winding.

clue.text: Power walk sports competition

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
to roam is to walk about

explanation.surface: A power walk is held as a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-am is a sporting tournament, often golf, in which professionals and amateurs play together.

clue.text: Young man's way with set control?

indicators.note: the letters of set are taken under control and arranged afresh, the question mark admitting this is loose

explanation.surface: A youth tries to keep a television set under control.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace Greeley's advice 'Go West, young man' supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase Go West, young man made the direction of the American frontier the path for an ambitious youth.

clue.text: Maybe pirate radio dropped one after speed distributed

indicators.note: the radio part comes after the speed part
the letters of speed are spread around in a new order
the radio word has dropped the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pirate radio station loses a single listener once its speeding broadcasts go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate radio' looks like one phrase, but 'Maybe pirate' is the definition and 'radio' is fodder for the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is one example of an outlaw or reckless criminal, which is what a desperado is.

clue.text: Possessing a lot of money, moved into expensive block

indicators.note: the shuffled letters possess, or hold within them, the money letter
the letters of into are moved around into a new order

parts.note: G stands for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone with plenty of cash has moved into a pricey apartment block.
explanation.walkthrough: INTO rearranged gives INOT, which holds G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of gold is a cast block of metal, and a very costly one.

clue.text: Bellow's last novel is Glass

parts.note: to bellow is to cry out

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of last get a new order

explanation.surface: Saul Bellow's final novel is titled Glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes the American novelist Saul Bellow, but bellow is a shout and novel signals the anagram of LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is a fine, clear kind of glass used for wine glasses and decanters.

clue.text: Spray over top of neglected church building

indicators.note: the spray device goes over, covering, the letter taken from neglected

parts.note: a mister is a spray bottle for plants

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Spraying the top of a church that has fallen into neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large church, such as York Minster.
